title: The Single-Stranded DNA-Binding Factor SUB1/PC4 Alleviates Replication Stress at Telomeres and is a Vulnerability of ALT Cancer Cells
authors: Jean-Christophe Dubois; Erin Bonnell; Julie Frion; Samuel Zimmer; Muhammad Riaz Khan; Gabriela M. Teplitz; Lisa Casimir; Élie Méthot; Amélie Filion; Mouhamed Idrissou; Pierre-Étienne Jacques; Raymund J. Wellinger; Alexandre Maréchal
one_liner_zh: 该文研究单链DNA结合蛋白SUB1/PC4在ALT癌细胞端粒复制应激缓解中的作用，涉及蛋白-ssDNA结合但非TF-DNA转录因子体系，且无AI或物理模拟建模方法，属边缘相关。
abstract: A bstract To achieve replicative immortality, cancer cells must activate telomere maintenance mechanisms. In 10-15% of cancers, this is enabled by recombination-based alternative lengthening of telomeres pathways (ALT). ALT cells display several hallmarks including heterogeneous telomere length, extrachromosomal telomeric repeats and ALT-associated PML bodies. ALT cells also have high telomeric replication stress (RS) enhanced by fork-stalling structures (R-loops, G4s) and altered chromatin states. In ALT cells, telomeric RS promotes telomere elongation but above a certain threshold becomes detrimental to cell survival. Manipulating RS at telomeres has thus been proposed as a therapeutic strategy against ALT cancers. Through analysis of genome-wide CRISPR fitness screens, we identified ALT-specific vulnerabilities and describe here our characterization of the roles of SUB1, a ssDNA-binding protein, as a novel regulator of telomere stability. SUB1 depletion further increases RS at ALT telomeres, profoundly impairing ALT cell growth without impacting telomerase-positive cancer cells. During RS, SUB1 is recruited to stalled forks and ALT telomeres via its ssDNA-binding domain. This recruitment is potentiated by RPA depletion, suggesting that these factors may compete for ssDNA. The viability of ALT cells and their resilience towards RS also requires ssDNA-binding by SUB1. SUB1 depletion accelerates cell death induced by FANCM depletion, triggering unsustainable levels of telomeric damage specifically in ALT cells. Finally, combining SUB1 depletion with RS-inducing drugs rapidly induces replication catastrophe in ALT cells. Altogether, our work identifies SUB1 as a new ALT susceptibility with important roles in the mitigation of RS at ALT telomeres and suggests new therapeutic strategies for a host of still poorly managed cancers. S ignificance S tatement Currently, there are few treatment options for ALT cancers with chemotherapy still occupying center stage despite often limited efficacy. ALT cancer cells experience high levels of replication stress at telomeres and its enhancement (e.g. via ATR inhibition) is a promising therapeutic strategy. Sensitivity to ATR inhibition varies amongst ALT cell lines/tumors warranting the development of additional ways to modulate telomeric replication stress. Here we identify SUB1, a single-stranded DNA-binding protein, as a vulnerability of ALT cells. SUB1 localizes to ALT telomeres and mitigates deleterious replication stress. SUB1 depletion synergizes with ATR inhibition and FANCM downregulation suggesting that co-targeting SUB1 with other regulators of replication stress at telomeres may kill ALT cancer cells more effectively.
abstract_zh:
摘要 为实现复制性永生，癌细胞必须激活端粒维持机制。在10-15%的癌症中，这一过程由基于重组的端粒延长替代途径（ALT）实现。ALT细胞表现出多种标志性特征，包括异质性端粒长度、染色体外端粒重复序列以及ALT相关PML小体。ALT细胞还承受高水平的端粒复制应激（RS），该应激因叉停滞结构（R-loops、G4s）和染色质状态改变而增强。在ALT细胞中，端粒RS促进端粒延长，但超过一定阈值后对细胞存活有害。因此，操纵端粒RS已被提议作为针对ALT癌症的治疗策略。通过对全基因组CRISPR适应性筛选的分析，我们识别出ALT特异性弱点，并在此描述我们对SUB1（一种单链DNA结合蛋白）作为端粒稳定性新型调节因子作用的表征。SUB1缺失进一步增加ALT端粒的RS，严重损害ALT细胞生长，而不影响端粒酶阳性癌细胞。在RS期间，SUB1通过其单链DNA结合域被招募至停滞叉和ALT端粒。这种招募因RPA缺失而增强，表明这些因子可能竞争单链DNA。ALT细胞的存活及其对RS的抵抗力也需要SUB1的单链DNA结合功能。SUB1缺失加速FANCM缺失诱导的细胞死亡，仅在ALT细胞中触发不可持续的端粒损伤水平。最后，将SUB1缺失与RS诱导药物联合使用可迅速在ALT细胞中引发复制灾难。总之，我们的工作将SUB1识别为一种新的ALT易感性因子，在缓解ALT端粒RS中发挥重要作用，并为多种仍难以管理的癌症提出新的治疗策略。

重要性声明 目前，ALT癌症的治疗选择有限，化疗尽管疗效常常有限，仍占据中心地位。ALT癌细胞在端粒处经历高水平的复制应激，增强该应激（例如通过ATR抑制）是一种有前景的治疗策略。对ATR抑制的敏感性在不同ALT细胞系/肿瘤中有所差异，这要求开发额外的方法来调节端粒复制应激。在此，我们识别出单链DNA结合蛋白SUB1作为ALT细胞的一个弱点。SUB1定位于ALT端粒并缓解有害的复制应激。SUB1缺失与ATR抑制和FANCM下调协同作用，表明同时靶向SUB1与其他端粒复制应激调节因子可能更有效地杀死ALT癌细胞。
